sentences.text: Psilopterus is an extinct genus of terror birds, a name derived from Greek meaning "naked wing", that inhabited Argentina and Uruguay from the Middle Oligocene to possibly the Late Pleistocene.
Members of this genus were relatively gracile and diminutive compared to other terror birds, making them among the smallest known species in the group.
Although they resembled modern cariama birds, Psilopterus possessed a heavier build and considerably smaller wings.
When standing on its head, the species P. bachmanni reached a height of 70 to 80 centimeters and weighed about 5 kilograms.
Key diagnostic features include a low skull and an upper jaw similar to that of mesembriornithine terror birds.
Fossil finds in Uruguay suggest this genus may have survived until approximately 96,040 ± 6,300 years ago.
The morphological similarity between the claws of cariamas and Psilopterus suggests they were used to strike prey, as both are sharp, curved, and laterally compressed.
The species P. lemoinei was slightly larger, with an estimated average weight of 7 kilograms.
The genus Psilopterus was described by Moreno and Mercerat in 1891.
The species and genus were defined based on a fused upper ankle and a foot bone, with the lectotype being a tarsometatarsus (MLP-168).
Specimens were found in 1899 in Chubut province, Argentina (Patagonia), in rocks dating from the middle to late Oligocene (Deseadense).
Psilopterus colzecus is known from a single incomplete skeleton including parts of the jaw, wing, and leg, with the holotype being MLP-76-VI-12-2.
It has been suggested that Psilopterus may have been able to fly briefly and clumsily, similar to extant seriemas, unlike larger terror birds.
Researchers suggest psilopterines likely preferred to run than fly, using flight primarily to reach treetops for nesting and protection from predators.
Researchers Tonni and Tambussi suggested Psilopterus could use its claws to climb trees and possibly fly, but this idea has been rejected in recent scientific literature.
Recent systematic revisions place Psilopterus within the subfamily Psilopterinae of the family Phorusrhacidae, alongside the genera Procariama and Paleopsilopterus.
The genus Psilopterus is divided into four species.
Psilopterus lived from the middle Oligocene to the late Pleistocene in Argentina.
The genus lived from the Aquitanian to the Late Pleistocene, approximately 23.04 to 0.0117 million years ago.
Psilopterus bachmanni and lemoinei lived during the Middle Miocene in the Santa Cruz Formation, inhabiting coastal, forested, and grassland regions.
During the Miocene, the climate in the region was similar to the coasts of Chile, featuring semi-temperate forests and oceanic winds.
The environment included large herbivorous notoungulates like Nesodon and Adinotherium as low browsers, and the frugivorous interatheriid Protypotherium.
Material of P. bachmanni comes from various sites in Santa Cruz province, Argentina, dating to the middle Miocene (Santacruciense).
Material of P. lemoinei has been found in sites in Santa Cruz province, Argentina, dating to the middle Miocene (Santacruciense).
Elements of P. colzecus were found in Buenos Aires province, Argentina, and date to the late Miocene (Chasiquense).
It is debated whether material currently assigned to P. lemoinei and P. bachmanni may be reclassified into separate species if reexamined in depth.
